edges.description: Supratentorial neural stem cells transformed by ZFTA-RELA fusion give rise to supratentorial ependymoma.
Supratentorial radial glial progenitors acquire YAP1 gene fusions (such as YAP1-MAMLD1) that define the ST-YAP1 molecular subgroup.
Hindbrain progenitors give rise to PFA ependymoma, which is defined by ectopic EZHIP overexpression.
Hindbrain progenitors in poor-prognosis PFA tumors acquire a CpG island methylator phenotype.
Transformed progenitors fail to complete neuronal-glial differentiation, establishing a tumor cellular hierarchy.
Retention of undifferentiated progenitor populations sustains tumor growth.
The fusion protein translocates to the nucleus and activates NF-kB target genes.
NF-kB target gene programs drive proliferation and survival of transformed progenitors.
Constitutive nuclear YAP1 fusion transcriptional activity drives supratentorial ependymal tumor growth.
EZHIP protein binds and inhibits the PRC2 catalytic subunit EZH2.
Loss of PRC2 catalytic activity prevents deposition and spreading of the H3K27me3 mark.
De-repression of PRC2 target neurodevelopmental genes prevents orderly lineage maturation.
De-repression and dysregulation of PRC2 target differentiation genes blocks normal lineage maturation.
Failure to silence differentiation programs maintains progenitors in a proliferative state.
Loss of merlin-mediated growth suppression permits progenitor expansion.
NF2-driven spinal ependymoma growth forms an intramedullary mass that compresses adjacent spinal cord tracts.
High-level MYCN amplification drives rapid tumor cell proliferation and malignant progression.
MYCN-amplified spinal ependymomas grow within the thoracic and cervical spine and infiltratively invade and compress the spinal cord.
MYCN-amplified spinal tumors infiltrate the spinal cord and disseminate through the CNS.
An enlarging posterior fossa or intraventricular mass obstructs CSF flow.
Tumor cells seed the leptomeninges via the cerebrospinal fluid.
Supratentorial cortical/periventricular mass growth irritates cerebral cortex and provokes epileptic seizures.
Posterior fossa mass expansion and brainstem/foramina of Luschka extension compress or infiltrate lower cranial nerves VI to X.
Intramedullary spinal ependymoma expansion compresses and thins surrounding spinal cord sensory, motor, and autonomic tracts.
Compression of intramedullary dorsal column and spinothalamic sensory pathways produces numbness and tingling.
Progressive thinning of corticospinal motor tracts by the intramedullary mass produces limb weakness.
Local dural and intramedullary distension and nerve root irritation produce axial and radicular back pain.
Autonomic and conus medullaris/cauda equina tract involvement causes early urinary sphincter dysfunction.
Obstructed CSF outflow raises intracranial pressure.
Fourth-ventricular or supratentorial ventricular obstruction directly causes non-communicating hydrocephalus.
Posterior fossa mass effect and obstructive fourth-ventricular distension impair cerebellar coordination, causing ataxia.
Elevated intracranial pressure produces progressive headache in older children and adults.
Raised intracranial pressure stimulates emetic centers, producing vomiting.
Transmitted intracranial hypertension along the optic nerve sheath causes optic disc swelling.
In infants and toddlers with open cranial sutures, raised intracranial pressure causes progressive head enlargement.

nodes.description: Ependymoma spreads through the cerebrospinal fluid rather than haematogenously. Leptomeningeal dissemination is present at diagnosis in up to 10% of intracranial cases, which is why staging includes craniospinal imaging and CSF cytology, and why craniospinal irradiation is reserved for documented metastatic disease.

evidence.snippet: Diagnosis requires histologic confirmation, aided by MRI and cerebrospinal fluid analysis, with dissemination present in up to 10% of cases at diagnosis.

nodes.description: Posterior fossa ependymomas characteristically arise in or extend into the fourth ventricle, where they obstruct cerebrospinal fluid pathways. The resulting non-communicating hydrocephalus and raised intracranial pressure produce the classic presenting syndrome of headache, vomiting and papilledema.

evidence.snippet: Clinical symptoms vary by location, with posterior fossa tumors often causing hydrocephalus-related signs, and supratentorial lesions presenting with seizures or focal deficits.

nodes.description: Focal conformal radiotherapy is recommended for grade 3 tumors and for incompletely resected grade 2 tumors. nodes.description: ZFTA-RELA fusion proteins localize spontaneously to the nucleus and constitutively activate canonical NF-kB target gene transcription, independently of upstream inflammatory signalling. This is a rare example of a recurrent genetic lesion directly activating NF-kB in human cancer, since constitutive NF-kB signalling is common in tumors but pathway mutations are otherwise rare. Mouse modelling indicates that additional driver functions beyond NF-kB contribute to tumorigenesis.

evidence.snippet: Although constitutive NF-κB signalling is present in most human tumours, mutations in pathway members are rare, complicating efforts to understand and block aberrant NF-κB activity in cancer.

nodes.description: Poor-prognosis hindbrain ependymomas independently exhibit a CpG island methylator phenotype (CIMP). Transcriptional silencing driven by CpG methylation converges on the same Polycomb repressive complex 2 targets, reinforcing the differentiation block. This epigenetic program, rather than recurrent point mutation, drives tumorigenesis — these tumors have an extremely low mutation rate with no significant recurrent somatic single nucleotide variants.

nodes.description: PFA ependymomas are characterized by global depletion of the repressive H3K27me3 mark, with loss of broad domains but retention at CpG islands. The resulting de-repression of PRC2 target genes is the defining epigenetic lesion of the group and is used diagnostically as an immunohistochemical surrogate.

nodes.description: Single-cell RNA sequencing shows that ependymomas are organized as a cellular hierarchy initiating from undifferentiated populations that undergo impaired differentiation toward three neuronal-glial lineages. The proportion of undifferentiated cells tracks with aggressiveness: favorable molecular groups are dominated by differentiated cells, whereas aggressive groups are enriched for undifferentiated populations.

nodes.description: The majority of supratentorial ependymomas harbor oncogenic fusions between RELA, the principal effector of canonical NF-kB signalling, and ZFTA (formerly C11orf95). These fusions arise by chromothripsis of chromosome 11q13.1 — a single catastrophic chromosomal shattering and reassembly event rather than stepwise mutation. This explains how a tumor with an otherwise very low mutation burden acquires a potent driver.
